tldr: Headlines split into two dominant registers: a neutral mission-completion announcement shared by most Western, Chinese, and Turkish outlets, and a triumphalist Iranian counter-narrative declaring the US 'expelled' and 'humiliated'. A minority of Western analytical headlines add a third register — post-withdrawal risk — while Russian outlets invoke the human cost of the original invasion.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to use 'expelled' — framing the departure as a coerced eviction rather than a negotiated withdrawal.
Only headline to pair withdrawal with ongoing US bombing of Iran — naming the policy contradiction no other title acknowledges.
Only Western headline to name a 'power vacuum' — framing the exit as strategic loss rather than mission completion.
Only headline to recast the moment as a deterrence declaration, not a troop-departure announcement.

bottom_line: The headline layer is dominated by neutral exit-announcement framing, but Iranian state outlets and Russia diverge sharply — labelling the withdrawal an 'expulsion', a 'humiliating defeat', and a new phase for the Resistance Front, vocabulary absent from every non-state-aligned headline.
